title: The Invoicing Lag: The Cash Flow Leak That Starts Before a Single Invoice Goes Unpaid
linkedin:
Most cash flow conversations start and end with slow-paying customers. Chase harder, tighten terms, follow up sooner.

That instinct isn't wrong. It's just missing half the picture.

There's a clock that starts running before the debtor clock ever begins: the time between finishing a job and actually sending the invoice. In owner-led businesses, that gap is rarely zero. Timesheets get collected, jobs get signed off, invoicing gets batched into a weekly or monthly run instead of happening the day the work finishes.

A five day invoicing lag sitting in front of a 30 day payment term isn't a 30 day wait for cash. It's a 35 day wait, and it never shows up on an aged debtor report, because the invoice has to exist before it can age.

The gap tends to widen exactly when a business can least afford it, when spring trading picks up and the admin behind raising invoices can't keep pace with the work itself.

The fix sits entirely inside the business. Pull ten recently completed jobs, compare completion date to invoice date, and average the gap. Most owners have never run this comparison. The number it surfaces is usually larger than expected.
